cards.name: Triple One to Many Round
cards.id: Brushes/Arrows/Pattern Arrows.ai#Triple One to Many Round
cards.summary: Pattern arrow brush: a thin dark monoline stroke whose end carries a small three-pronged fork, the crow's-foot 'one to many' mark of entity-relationship diagrams; the start is a plain cut end. The thumbnail shows a single line, not three, so 'Triple' reads as the three prongs; what 'Round' refers to is not visible at this size. Rendered by script (brush applied to a 300 pt S-curve at 1 pt stroke), not a shipped preview.
use_for: entity-relationship or database diagram connectors (one-to-many relation)
org-chart or flow lines that fan out to several items
avoid: solid arrows or pointers for marketing art: the fork reads as notation, not direction; use Yellow Arrow Brush or Stroke panel arrowheads
paths drawn the wrong way: the fork lands on the last anchor, reverse the path direction (Object > Path > Reverse Path Direction) to flip it

Brushes only apply inside a document that holds them: a script must app.open the library, apply the brush to an item there and duplicate that item into the target document (use the Brush Libraries panel by hand)
cards.applies_to: an open path item; the pattern brush tiles its side tile along the path and places its end tile at the path's last anchor, so path direction decides where the arrowhead lands
cards.how_to_apply: By hand: select a path, Window > Brush Libraries > Arrows > Pattern Arrows, click 'Triple One to Many Round' (it is added to the Brushes panel and applied). By script: app.open("C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Illustrator 2026/Presets/en_US/Brushes/Arrows/Pattern Arrows.ai"), doc.brushes.getByName("Triple One to Many Round").applyTo(pathItem) on a path there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) to carry the brush into the target document, then close the Pattern Arrows library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Single thin black line, plain cut start, three-pronged crow's-foot fork on the end anchor.

cards.name: Yellow Arrow Brush
cards.summary: Pattern arrow brush: a narrow pale-yellow band with a thin dark grey outline that runs the length of the path, starting from a small squared tail and ending in a small solid yellow arrowhead with a dark outline. Bright, cartoon-like pointer line. Rendered by script (brush applied to a 300 pt S-curve at 1 pt stroke), not a shipped preview.
use_for: curved pointer arrows on tutorials, how-to graphics and annotated screenshots
playful direction cues on posters and maps
callout arrows that must stay readable on dark or busy backgrounds thanks to the dark outline
avoid: colour-matched brand arrows: the yellow and outline are baked into the tiles, it does not follow the stroke colour; use a calligraphic or plain stroke with Stroke panel arrowheads instead
very small artwork: at 1 pt the band and head are tiny, raise the stroke weight to scale the tiles up
